# EDA and Data cleaning

Sources: 
- Macroeconomic predictors: https://www.stevanovic.uqam.ca/DS_LCMD.html 
- Canadian CPI: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401 (check at 8:30pm)
- FRED-MD data: https://www.stlouisfed.org/research/economists/mccracken/fred-databases 

References:

Fortin-Gagnon, O., Leroux, M., Stevanovic, D. and Surprenant, S. (2022), A large Canadian database for macroeconomic analysis. Canadian Journal of Economics/Revue canadienne d'économique, 55: 1799-1833. https://doi.org/10.1111/caje.12618 

Statistics Canada. Table 18-10-0004-01  Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted. DOI: https://doi.org/10.25318/1810000401-eng

## Data is obtained from:

**August 2026** zip file downloaded from the data source

readme.txt content: 

These files contain datasets used in: 
Fortin-Gagnon, Leroux, Stevanovic and Surprenant (2018) A Large Canadian Data for Macroeconomic Analysis.

- `CAN_MD.xlsx`: raw data as collected from StatCan. It starts from 1914 because the CPI series is available from that year
- `TR_CAN_MD.xlsx`: data from CAN_MD.xlsx transformed to induce stationarity.
- `balanced_can_md.xlsx`: stationary and balanced panel starting from 1981M01. Missing values are replaced by EM algorithm. 
- `Table_can_md.xlsx`: detailed data description

We use `balanced_can_md.xlsx` as the data is already stationary and balanced panel. 

From `Table_can_md.xlsx` we can see that the following variables are discontinued and ends in September 2020. we should remove these from the data source 
- `CRED_T-discontinued`
- `CRED_HOURS_discontinued`
- `CRED_MORT_discontinued`
- `CRED_CONS_discontinued`
- `CRED_BUS_discontinued`

## Canadian Macroeconomic indicators data

```{r}
# import canadian macroeconomic indicators data
can_md <- read_csv("data/raw/balanced_can_md.csv")

# inspect can_md
dim(can_md)
names(can_md)
head(can_md) # data starts from 1981-01-01
tail(can_md) # last data is 2026-07-01
```

```{r}
# check missing values
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(can_md))
missing_count[missing_count > 0]
sum(is.na(can_md))

# check duplicates 
sum(duplicated(can_md$Date))
range(can_md$Date)

# check date range, if every month is present
nrow(can_md)
expected_dates <- seq(
  min(can_md$Date),
  max(can_md$Date),
  by = "month"
)
setdiff(expected_dates, can_md$Date)
```

```{r}
discontinued_vars <- c(
  "CRED_T_discontinued",
  "CRED_HOUS_discontinued",
  "CRED_MORT_discontinued",
  "CRED_CONS_discontinued",
  "CRE_BUS_discontinued"
)

intersect(discontinued_vars, names(can_md))
can_md <- can_md %>%
  select(-any_of(discontinued_vars))

# check whether removed
sum(is.na(can_md))
```

```{r}
# rename variables to standardise across datasets
can_md <- can_md %>%
  rename(date = Date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  arrange(date)

class(can_md$date)
range(can_md$date)
sum(duplicated(can_md$date))
```

## CPI Data
Testing unseasonally adjusted data -> ARIMA adjustment -> compare against officially seasonally adjusted data. Unsure of which one to use... 

```{r}
# import canadian CPI data
cpi_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/1810000401_databaseLoadingData.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cpi_official_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/1810000601_databaseLoadingData.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# clean column headers
cpi <- cpi_raw %>%
  transmute(
    date = as.Date(paste0(REF_DATE, "-01")),
    cpi = as.numeric(VALUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)

cpi_official <- cpi_official_raw %>%
  transmute(
    date = as.Date(paste0(REF_DATE, "-01")),
    cpi_official = as.numeric(VALUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)
```

```{r}
head(cpi)
tail(cpi)

range(cpi$date)
range(cpi_official$date)

sum(duplicated(cpi$date))
sum(duplicated(cpi_official$date))
```

Since the data is not seasonally adjusted, we use `X-13ARIMA-SEATS` to seasonally adjust. 

```{r}
# check for regularly spaced time series
cpi_ts <- ts(
  cpi$cpi,
  start = c(
    year(min(cpi$date)),
    month(min(cpi$date))
  ),
  frequency = 12
)

start(cpi_ts)
end(cpi_ts)
frequency(cpi_ts)
```

```{r}
# to seasonally adjust our CPI, we use ARIMA
# Estimate seasonal adjustment
sa_model <- seas(
  cpi_ts,
  x11 = ""
)

# Extract seasonally adjusted CPI
cpi_sa <- final(sa_model)

# Examine model
summary(sa_model)

# Plot results
plot(sa_model)
```

```{r}
cpi_adjusted <- data.frame(
  date = cpi$date,
  cpi_unadjusted = cpi$cpi,
  cpi_adjusted = as.numeric(cpi_sa)
)
```

```{r}
comparison <- cpi_adjusted %>%
  inner_join(cpi_official, by = "date")

range(comparison$date)
nrow(comparison)
```

```{r}
# plot self-adjusted and officially adjusted
comparison_long <- comparison %>%
  select(date, cpi_adjusted, cpi_official) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "cpi"
  )

ggplot(comparison_long,
       aes(x = date, y = cpi, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Seasonally Adjusted Canadian CPI",
    x = "Year",
    y = "CPI Index",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# compare inflation rates
comparison <- comparison %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    inflation_self =
      1200 * (log(cpi_adjusted) -
              log(lag(cpi_adjusted))),

    inflation_official =
      1200 * (log(cpi_official) -
              log(lag(cpi_official)))
  )

ggplot(comparison, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = inflation_self, color = "Self-adjusted")
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = inflation_official, color = "Official")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Inflation: Self-adjusted vs Official",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annualised Inflation (%)",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# quantitative analysis
valid <- comparison %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(inflation_self),
    !is.na(inflation_official)
  )

errors <- valid$inflation_self -
          valid$inflation_official

mae <- mean(abs(errors))
rmse <- sqrt(mean(errors^2))
bias <- mean(errors)

correlation <- cor(
  valid$inflation_self,
  valid$inflation_official
)

data.frame(
  MAE = mae,
  RMSE = rmse,
  Bias = bias,
  Correlation = correlation
)
```

## Fred Data

```{r}
# import fred-md
fred_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/2026-rev-08-MD.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

head(fred_raw)
```

```{r}
# preserve transformation codes
fred_transform <- fred_raw[1, ] 
fred_transform
```

```{r}
fred_md <- fred_raw %>%
  slice(-1) %>%                     # remove transformation codes
  rename(date = sasdate) %>%        # rename column to standardise
  mutate(date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")) %>%
  filter(date >= as.Date("1981-01-01"))
```

```{r}
dim(fred_md)
names(fred_md)
head(fred_md) 
tail(fred_md)
```

## Constructing our target 

** Need to decide which metric to use

```{r}
# constructing our variable - inflation 
cpi_model <- cpi_adjusted %>%
  transmute(
    date,
    cpi_sa = cpi_adjusted,
    log_cpi = log(cpi_adjusted),
    inflation_mom = 1200 *
      (log_cpi - lag(log_cpi))
  )

# constructing three-month-ahead average inflation target 
# ie. using January 2020 predictor information to forecast inflation from Jan-April 2020

cpi_model <- cpi_model %>%
  mutate(
    target_h3 = 400 *
      (lead(log_cpi, 3) - log_cpi)
  )
```

## Time to merge

Note: CPI model is using self-seasonally adjusted

```{r}
# All datasets must have a column named "date"
can_md$date <- as.Date(can_md$date)
fred_md$date <- as.Date(fred_md$date)
cpi_model$date <- as.Date(cpi_model$date)

# Check duplicate dates
sum(duplicated(can_md$date))
sum(duplicated(fred_md$date))
sum(duplicated(cpi_model$date))

# Check coverage
range(can_md$date)
range(cpi_model$date)
range(fred_md$date)

dim(can_md)
dim(cpi_model)
dim(fred_md)
```

### Main analysis: Canadian macroeconomic indicators + CPI `main_data`

```{r}
main_data <- can_md %>%
  inner_join(
    cpi_model,
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)

dim(main_data)
head(main_data)
```

### Secondary analysis: Fred data + Canadian macroeconomic indicators + CPI `extended_data`

Note: should choose indicators that would be useful, and rename with "US" prefix to avoid confusion

```{r}
extended_data <- main_data %>%
  left_join(
    fred_md,
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)

dim(extended_data)
head(extended_data)
```

```{r}
# save data 
dir.create(
  "data/processed",
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

saveRDS(
  main_data,
  "data/processed/main_data.rds"
)

saveRDS(
  extended_data,
  "data/processed/extended_data.rds"
)
```
